title: Swietenine improved the progression of diabetic nephropathy through inhibiting ferroptosis via activating Akt/GSK-3beta/Nrf2 signaling pathway.
authors: Duan, Jingyu; Pei, Feilong; Miao, Jiale; Liu, Shuang; Tan, Lin; Lu, Mengyuan; Liu, Yaowu; Zhang, Chunping
one_liner_zh: 该文研究天然化合物Swietenine通过Akt/GSK-3beta/Nrf2通路抑制铁死亡改善糖尿病肾病，属纯药理与湿实验研究，无蛋白质-DNA互作体系、无结合建模、无AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Swietenia macrophylla King is a traditional medicinal plant extensively utilized in Asia and its pharmacological properties primarily involve antidiabetic, anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, antibacterial, and antitumor effects. Swietenine (Swi), the major bioactive compound presents in the fruits of S. macrophylla, has demonstrated beneficial therapeutic effects on diabetic nephropathy (DN). However, the underlying mechanism through which Swi influences DN remains unclear. AIM OF THE STUDY: The current research aims to investigate the effects of Swi on DN and explore its underlying mechanisms associated with ferroptosis, both in vivo and in vitro. METHODS: A model of streptozotocin/high-fat diet (STZ/HFD)-induced Sprague-Dawley (SD) rats was employed to assess the effect of Swi on improving DN and resisting ferroptosis in vivo. Additionally, mouse podocyte cells (MPC-5 cells) were induced by high glucose (HG) and cultured to explore the potential mechanisms of Swi in treating DN in vitro. To further validate the protective effects of Swi, pathway-specific inhibitors were administered to HG-induced MPC-5 cells to confirm the involvement of the Akt/GSK-3beta/Nrf2 signaling pathway in the inhibition of ferroptosis. A combination of proteomics, immunohistochemical staining, western blotting, and cell culture techniques was utilized to explore the pharmacological mechanisms of Swi. Furthermore, network pharmacology and molecular docking analyses were conducted to predict the targets of Swi in relation to DN, which were subsequently validated through Western blotting analysis. RESULTS: Administration of Swi significantly enhanced renal function and ameliorated pathological alterations in DN rats, as well as improved oxidative stress and inhibited ferroptosis. In vitro studies revealed that Swi dramatically improved the cell viability and mitigated oxidative stress, and inhibited ferroptosis via activating the Akt/GSK-3beta/Nrf2 signaling pathway in HG-induced MPC-5 cells. CONCLUSION: This study demonstrates that Swi improves DN by inhibiting ferroptosis via activating Akt/GSK-3beta/Nrf2 signaling pathway for the first time, thereby providing a scientific basis that Swi is expected to be a promising candidate drug for the treatment of DN.
abstract_zh: 民族药理学相关性：大叶桃花心木（Swietenia macrophylla King）是一种在亚洲广泛使用的传统药用植物，其药理特性主要包括抗糖尿病、抗炎、抗氧化、抗菌和抗肿瘤作用。Swi（Swietenine）是大叶桃花心木果实中存在的主要生物活性化合物，已被证明对糖尿病肾病（DN）具有有益的治疗效果。然而，Swi影响DN的潜在机制仍不清楚。研究目的：本研究旨在探讨Swi对DN的影响，并在体内和体外条件下探索其与铁死亡相关的潜在机制。方法：采用链脲佐菌素/高脂饮食（STZ/HFD）诱导的Sprague-Dawley（SD）大鼠模型，评估Swi在体内改善DN和抵抗铁死亡的作用。此外，通过高糖（HG）诱导小鼠足细胞（MPC-5细胞）并培养，以探索Swi在体外治疗DN的潜在机制。为进一步验证Swi的保护作用，对HG诱导的MPC-5细胞给予通路特异性抑制剂，以确认Akt/GSK-3beta/Nrf2信号通路参与铁死亡的抑制。结合蛋白质组学、免疫组织化学染色、蛋白质印迹和细胞培养技术，探索Swi的药理机制。此外，通过网络药理学和分子对接分析预测Swi与DN相关的靶点，并通过蛋白质印迹分析进行验证。结果：给予Swi显著改善了DN大鼠的肾功能和病理变化，同时改善了氧化应激并抑制了铁死亡。体外研究表明，Swi显著提高了细胞活力，减轻了氧化应激，并通过激活HG诱导的MPC-5细胞中的Akt/GSK-3beta/Nrf2信号通路抑制了铁死亡。结论：本研究首次证明Swi通过激活Akt/GSK-3beta/Nrf2信号通路抑制铁死亡来改善DN，从而为Swi有望成为治疗DN的候选药物提供了科学依据。
